bib.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), ACL 2022

question: How much duplicated text do common LM training sets contain, and does removing it change perplexity, memorization and train-test leakage?
hypothesis: Deduplicating training data reduces memorized output and train-test overlap without hurting perplexity.
contributions: Two scalable deduplication tools: EXACTSUBSTR (suffix array) and NEARDUP (MinHash)
Measurement of duplication in C4, RealNews, LM1B, Wiki-40B
Showing deduplicated training reduces memorization ~10x and keeps or improves perplexity
Quantifying train-test leakage effect on released models

method.summary: Deduplicate C4, RealNews, LM1B and Wiki-40B with exact 50-token substring matching via suffix arrays and with MinHash plus edit similarity >0.8, then train 1.5B (XL) and 110M (base) T5-codebase decoder-only LMs on original and deduplicated C4 and compare perplexity and memorization in sampled text.
method.task: dataset deduplication; causal LM pretraining on C4; memorization measurement

datasets.name: C4
datasets.size: 360M web documents, avg 486 BPE tokens; 364.87M examples / 177.3B tokens (Table 13)
datasets.preprocessing: Original paragraph-hash dedup; NearDup leaves 350.48M examples / 173.7B tokens; ExactSubstr 350.48M examples / 165.4B tokens

training.objective: inferred: next-token prediction (decoder-only LM, perplexity evaluated)
training.hardware: 128-core TPU v3 pod slice (XL); 64-core TPU v3 pod slice (base)
training.compute: XL: 16804.70 TPU hrs original, 16149.31 ExactSubstr, 5.86/5.63 MWh; base 1.61 MWh (Table 6)
training.wall_clock: XL ~131 h (original, ExactSubstr), ~126 h (NearDup); base ~3 days
training.seeds: 3 random seeds per dataset for base models (9 base models); XL single run

inference.samples: 100,000 sequences per setting; five prompt types x two checkpoints, 1M sequences per model
inference.prompting: no prompt, or first 32 tokens of train-dup, train-unique, valid-in-train, valid-unique examples

parameters.exactsubstr_k: 50 BPE tokens (suffix array on bytes of BPE tokens)
parameters.memorized_token_rule: token part of a 50-token substring exactly in training data

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: validation perplexity on C4 Original, C4 Unique (no NearDup match), C4 Duplicates (NearDup match in train), LM1B, Wiki-40B

metrics.name: Memorized token rate
metrics.definition: % generated tokens that are part of a 50-token substring exactly in training data

metrics.name: Continuation match
metrics.definition: fraction of generations with edit similarity >0.8 to ground-truth continuation for 32-token prompts

eval.protocol: 3 seeds for base models; one XL run per dataset; perplexity compared on validation subsets; no significance test stated

limits: No downstream-task evaluation; only perplexity and memorization.
EXACTSUBSTR and NEARDUP use different thresholds; a different choice could change the comparison (Sec 6.1).
Does not distinguish harmful from innocuous memorization; no privacy study.
Does not study negative consequences of deduplication (tasks needing memorization, loss of attribution).
Deduplicated models still copy ground truth more often from duplicate prompts, so more stringent dedup may be needed.
English datasets only; XL models trained once (no seeds), base models 3 seeds.
Deduplication is not sufficient to remove private data.
Dataset size reduction: abstract says up to 19% smaller (RealNews tokens), App D says 3.9% for the C4 runs.

terms.definition: remove substrings of at least k=50 tokens shared verbatim by more than one example, found with a suffix array
MinHash-based approximate matching of whole documents, followed by edit similarity >0.8 filter
